messages:
alexa (sre): seeing huge DNS p95 spikes in eu-west-2 starting ~11:12UTC, GPU job queue is stalling, pods retrying connect loops
raj (infra): saw that too, CoreDNS logs show repeated timeouts + UDP truncation on replies. putting a quick `dig +time=2` against cluster IP shows intermittent no-answer
emily (oncall): alert fired: `service-resolve-failure` on gpu-pool, autoscaler noticed and started spin-up, then new nodes hit readiness checks that error out because sidecars can't resolve internal services
marco (ml infra): impact: long-running jobs hit 504s talking to model-store, shapes job backpressure -> cost goes up as autoscaler ramps then cools repeatedly :/
alexa (sre): grabbing tcpdump from a troubled node now, but early sign: lots of UDP retransmits and `ICMP fragmented` in dmesg. not classic MTU constant failure though, looks bursty
kevin (platform): could be SNAT port exhaustion on NAT gateway or conntrack churn. busy GPU pods open many short-lived connections to internal endpoints which amplifies UDP queries
raj (infra): confirming conntrack table near 100% on a few nodes, ephemeral port reuse high. I see `nf_conntrack` evicting entries and then coredns queries getting dropped or reordered
emily (oncall): paste of `ss -s` from node: 
```
State          Recv-Q Send-Q
TCP:   1024      0      0
UDP:     4200 packets
Sockets: used 27800, unuseable 0
```
(not exact, but the conntrack util is >90%)
alexa (sre): also seeing DNS NXDOMAIN cache churn from our node-local cache: a lot of negative entries get cached then evicted causing repeated upstream queries -> amplifies load to CoreDNS pods
marco (ml infra): hypothesis: autoscaler + model-store retries open many short TCP/UDP sessions while resolving, causing conntrack churn -> SNAT ports run low -> subsequent packets get blackholed -> look like DNS timeouts
raj (infra): quick mitigation ideas: 1) increase conntrack and nf_conntrack_max on affected nodepool 2) add additional coredns replicas on eu-west-2 3) add a short-term NAT scaling or move to per-node SNAT to reduce central gateway pressure 4) temporarily throttle autoscaler backoff so we don't amplify churn
kevin (platform): agree. also we should enable DNS caching sidecar for the model-store deployment (keep TTLs short) so we avoid repeated upstream UDP queries during spikes
emily (oncall): executing: bump conntrack on gpu-nodepool via kube-ssh (will patch DaemonSet sysctl) and roll coredns to +2 replicas. I'll also flip autoscaler to 30s cooldown to avoid ripples. ETA 12m
sre-bot: deploy started: sysctl-daemonset-patch -> progressing
alexa (sre): running `tcpdump -n udp port 53` capture shows lots of `udp src=10.2.x.x:random dst=10.3.y.y:53` followed by `ICMP port unreachable` from gateway occasionally — consistent with SNAT port limit/overflow
raj (infra): looking at NAT instance metrics: ephemeral ports used spikes at the same timestamps as the alerts. scaling NAT pool up in the cloud now and switching a subset of traffic to elastic IPs to spread the allocation
marco (ml infra): parallel effort: add a local in-memory cache to model-store (30s TTL) and add jittered retries in client library to avoid synchronized reconnection storms
kevin (platform): long-term action items: instrument per-pod ephemeral port usage, consider per-node SNAT (or eBPF SNAT) to reduce centralization, update SRE runbook for DNS+conntrack failures, and run a chaos test for port exhaustion
emily (oncall): monitoring dashboards show p95 DNS latency dropping back to normal after conntrack bump and NAT scale. I'll keep watch for 30m and then revert autoscaler cooldown if stable
alexa (sre): thanks all. postmortem notes: root cause likely ephemeral port/conntrack exhaustion amplifying DNS failures -> coredns timeouts -> autoscaler oscillation. mitigation worked: conntrack bump + NAT scaling + localized caching. follow-up: run a week-long stress test and add alert for conntrack >80%
kevin (platform): logging follow-up task in infra backlog. assigning to raj for root-cause deep dive and to marco for client-side hardening. :thumbsup:
emily (oncall): closing alert for now, will reopen if recurrence
